timeline.query: anybody at eth doing anything for people with disabilizes?

timeline.draft_answer: Yes. ETH Zurich runs a "Barrier-free ETH" / accessibility programme aimed at improving access to its buildings and services for people with disabilities or special needs, including students, teachers, researchers, staff and visitors. The programme is structured into 14 subprojects across three categories: "construction, building usage and architecture", "organisation and culture", and "technology, communication and teaching". Concrete measures include expanded accessible public tours (with icons indicating whether tours are wheelchair-accessible, suited for people with visual impairments, or available with a sign-language interpreter) — for example a "joining with wood" tour designed for visually impaired visitors. Facility Management also carries out regular inspection rounds to remove movable obstacles (blocked ramps, corridors, fire doors). Leadership (the Vice President of HR and Resources) frames this as a social duty, and work on an inclusive-university mission statement is being folded into a new holistic ETH Diversity Strategy from 2022. The chunks don't detail every specific service (e.g., individual student support offerings).
